items.title: Ensoma cuts jobs, narrows focus to lead asset
items.snippet: Follow along as BioSpace tracks job cuts and restructuring initiatives.

items.title: Replimune to ride wave of physician support to launch advanced melanoma therapy
items.snippet: Analysts expect Replimune’s newly approved Tudriqev to reach $1.3 billion in peak sales in 2035.

items.title: 2026 Q2 Job Market Report: Job postings keep rising as fewer companies cut employees
items.snippet: Job postings increase and competition dips, according to BioSpace data.

items.title: Intellia finds genetic suspect for liver safety signals with ATTR gene therapy
items.snippet: In November 2025, one patient died after receiving Intellia Therapeutics’ investigational gene silencer for transthyretin amyloidosis.

items.title: Vistagen’s repeat-dose anxiety nasal spray can’t beat placebo in mid-stage study
items.snippet: The Phase 2 study was small and was not designed to establish the statistical difference between Vistagen’s drug candidate and placebo, according to Vistagen. The biotech plans to meet with the FDA to determine a registrational path for the asset.

items.title: Third time’s the charm for Replimune as melanoma drug earns FDA greenlight
items.snippet: Replimune’s immunotherapy for advanced melanoma faced a perilous regulatory road with two previous rejections, but the drug—to be marketed as Tudriqev—prevailed with strong support from oncologists and a 10-3 advisory committee vote in its favor.

items.title: BioVie shares halve on murky Parkinson’s disease readout
items.snippet: BioVie’s stock fell by nearly 50% as the biotech claimed victory in a mid-stage Parkinson’s disease trial using an alternative endpoint to the primary clinical goal.

items.title: Braveheart pumps more life into biotech IPO market with $382M expected debut
items.snippet: Braveheart Bio has emerged on the Nasdaq with an upsized expected initial public offering—marking the public entrance of the twenty-second biotech this year.

items.title: Takeda’s narcolepsy nod opens orexin doors
items.snippet: Orzeyful is the first orexin agonist cleared by the FDA, and is the first narcolepsy therapy that addresses the full host of disease symptoms. It is "likely to reshape the treatment paradigm” for the condition, Jefferies told investors.

items.title: Sanofi pauses mid-stage lung study amid new CEO’s ‘rigorous portfolio prioritization’
items.snippet: Since stepping in as Sanofi’s CEO in April, Belén Garijo has launched a deep look at the pharma’s pipeline, reassessing assets based on “scientific merit” and potential for long-term value in the quest for a Dupixent follow-up.

items.title: Moderna’s flu shot crosses FDA finish line, bouncing back from regulatory roadblock
items.snippet: The FDA in February slapped Moderna’s vaccine with a refusal-to-file letter—though the agency backtracked a few days later and accepted a revised submission for review. An advisory committee in June unanimously backed mFLUVISA’s approval.

items.title: LifeMine raises $263M in mission to improve organ transplant aftercare
items.snippet: Patients who receive an organ transplant must take difficult immuno-suppressive medicines for the rest of their lives. LifeMine Therapeutics wants to offer a safer alternative.

items.title: The next treatment-resistant depression paradigm
items.snippet: In this episode of Denatured, you’ll hear from Hans Eriksson, chief medical officer at FundaMental Pharma and Steve Levine, chief patient officer at Compass Pathways. We explore why treatment-resistant depression remains so difficult to address, and how new approaches—from rapid-acting antidepressants to psychedelic t...

items.title: The top 12 companies hiring in biopharma now
items.snippet: Looking for a biopharma job? Check out the BioSpace list of 12 top companies hiring life sciences professionals like you.

items.title: CROs vs. biotechs: Finding the right fit
items.snippet: While biotechs and contract research organizations each have their advantages, that doesn’t mean both options work for everyone. Two experts discuss the differing environments and how to pick between them.

items.title: Lilly confident in slow and steady Foundayo launch, as ex-US sales shine
items.snippet: Foundayo clocked $98 million in sales in Q2, the first quarter it was available, compared to Novo’s $355 million for the same sales period.

items.title: Lilly, FDA retatrutide biologic dispute comes to a head as submission nears
items.snippet: A legal dispute between the FDA and Eli Lilly over whether the highly anticipated obesity candidate retatrutide is indeed a biologic has come to a head as the company prepares to submit the medicine for approval.

items.title: No deal between AstraZeneca and BMS, senior source insists: Reuters
items.snippet: Reuters has deflated rumors that AstraZeneca and Bristol Myers Squibb are discussing a possible merger, letting the air out of industry-wide speculation over what could have been the largest deal in pharma history.

items.title: Bespoke gene-editing outfit abandons lead program, cuts ‘several’ employees
items.snippet: Seven months after launching with $16 million in seed financing, Jennifer Doudna’s Aurora Therapeutics is pivoting away from its lead indication, phenylketonuria, owing to growing competition in the field.

items.title: Over 1/3 stay in biopharma jobs for health insurance, poll finds
items.snippet: A recruiter and career coach discuss when and why some biotech and pharma professionals put a premium on health insurance benefits.

items.title: Chaotic adcomms threaten to derail FDA’s bid to renew trust after Makary, Prasad
items.snippet: The FDA has been trying to mend fences with rare disease drug developers and patient groups since the departure of former Commissioner Marty Makary three months ago. But advisory committee meetings last week for Replimune and Capricor Therapeutics only created more confusion and frustration.

items.title: Biotech’s China problem: An issue of national security or economic value for the US?
items.snippet: Congressional letters sent to the CEOs of Eli Lilly, Pfizer, Merck, BMS and AbbVie this week voicing concerns about the pharmas' clinical trials in China highlight an ongoing discrepancy in how government and industry think about the rise of the Asian country’s biotech industry.

items.title: BIO 2026: Cell and gene therapy sector must break the mold to thrive
items.snippet: If cell and gene therapy makers are going to achieve their mission to improve patients’ lives, the industry must come together to share information across stakeholders, from regulators to manufacturers to payers.

items.title: At FDA, ‘caretaker mode’ is better than power trip mode
items.snippet: UniQure’s planned third-quarter submission for its Huntington’s disease gene therapy may be a harbinger of a more flexible FDA under acting commissioner Kyle Diamantas—but how long will it last? And how can companies be sure these positive decisions won’t just be reversed?
